note: Hand-authored fixture. Product demo: the rep walks Marcus through notes generated from his own recording, following the discovery call.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Right, I've got the call you sent. Before I share, how well do you remember it?

segments.speaker: Prospect
segments.text: Reasonably. That's the one where he wouldn't commit to anything.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Perfect, because that's the test. If I show you something wrong you'll spot it straight away.

segments.speaker: Prospect
segments.text: Go on then.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Let me just — can you see my screen?

segments.speaker: Prospect
segments.text: Yep, got it.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Okay. So, four objections, three next steps, one read on intent.

segments.speaker: Prospect
segments.text: Hm. Second one down. That's — yeah, that's almost word for word what he said.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Click it.

segments.speaker: Prospect
segments.text: Oh. Right, it jumps to the line.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Every claim does that. There isn't a line in there that isn't attached to something someone actually said.

segments.speaker: Prospect
segments.text: And when it's not sure?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: It drops it. And it tells you it dropped it, there's a count at the top.

segments.speaker: Prospect
segments.text: So it'd rather show me less.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Always. Because the alternative is you find one wrong thing and then you don't trust any of it.

segments.speaker: Prospect
segments.text: Which is exactly what happened to us. One bad summary and the team was done.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: So — anything in there you'd argue with?

segments.speaker: Prospect
segments.text: Give me a sec.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Take your time.

segments.speaker: Prospect
segments.text: No. No, actually. And it's got the procurement freeze thing, which I'd completely forgotten about.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: That one's about thirty minutes in, it's quite buried.

segments.speaker: Prospect
segments.text: That's genuinely useful. That would've cost me a call to find.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: So what would stop you rolling this out?

segments.speaker: Prospect
segments.text: Two things. It's got to land in the CRM. My reps aren't going to go looking for another tab, they just won't.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah. That's the second most common thing we hear, after trust. The HubSpot push is on the roadmap, it isn't built yet.

segments.speaker: Prospect
segments.text: Mm. That's a real gap for us. It's not a no, but I'd want a date.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: That's fair. I'd rather come back with a date than make one up now.

segments.speaker: Prospect
segments.text: And the other thing's the number, obviously. I did look at the pricing page.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, I'd rather do that properly with the numbers in front of us than dodge it on a call.

segments.speaker: Prospect
segments.text: Alright. Then let's get Dave from finance on.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: That's the right next step. What does he need to see?

segments.speaker: Prospect
segments.text: What we stop paying for, and what the reps get back in time. And it needs to be one page, he won't read past page one.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: One page. When suits?

segments.speaker: Prospect
segments.text: Thursday or Friday, I'll check his calendar and send an invite.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: I'll have the page ready either way.
